papers.title: Association Between Anorexia Nervosa Severity and Social and Occupational Functioning across Adulthood
papers.abstract: Importance: Severe anorexia nervosa (AN) carries substantial mortality risk, but its consequences associated with social and occupational functioning remain poorly characterized, limiting the development of targeted interventions to improve functioning, prevent and reduce long-term social disadvantage. Objective: To determine whether AN severity is associated with educational attainment, employment, income, and cohabitation status. Design: Cohort study following social and occupational outcomes across adulthood until age 55. Setting: Population-based. Participants: All individuals born in Denmark from 1963 to 1994, alive and residing in Denmark at age 30. The AN group had a first AN diagnosis between ages 10 and 25 years, excluding those who died or emigrated within 5 years. The comparison group had no AN diagnosis. Exposure: Illness severity of AN, measured by the AN Register-based Severity Index 5 years after the first AN diagnosis. Main Outcomes and Measures: Educational attainment was assessed at age 25 (upper secondary education) and at age 30/35 (highest completed education). Employment status, income deficiency, and cohabitation status were assessed annually from age 30 to 55. Results: Among 2,442,916 individuals, 9,465 were diagnosed with AN, of whom 1,996 (21.1%) were classified as severe AN cases. At age 25, individuals with severe AN had increased odds of non-completion of upper-secondary education compared to the general population (odds ratio [OR]=3.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.72-3.46), and those with less severe AN (OR=1.39; 95% CI: 1.29-1.50). At age 30, severe AN was associated with higher odds of unemployment (OR=3.42; 95% CI: 3.03-3.86), income deficiency (OR=3.84; 95% CI: 3.42-4.31), and living alone (OR=2.43; 95% CI: 2.17-2.71) compared to the less severe AN group. The risk of unemployment and income deficiency diverged across time: individuals with less severe AN gradually approached the general population, whereas those with severe AN diverged further over time. Within the AN cohort, severity differences persisted after adjustment for active AN diagnosis, with minimal attenuation. Conclusions and Relevance: Greater lifetime AN severity was associated with significantly poorer long-term social and occupational functioning outcomes, and these functional difficulties may persist beyond periods of active illness. This vulnerable group needs substantial support in these areas throughout the course of illness.

papers.title: Genomic epidemiology reconstructs the pre-detection transmission and establishment of chikungunya virus in Guangdong, China
papers.abstract: In 2025, a chikungunya outbreak in southern China resulted in more than 25,000 confirmed cases, but its origins and transmission history remain unresolved. As part of the public health investigation, we generated 1,264 near-complete chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomes from Guangdong Province and integrated genomic, epidemiological, entomological, and human mobility data to reconstruct the emergence and spread of this outbreak. Our analyses traced the outbreak to a single dominant introduction of a Reunion-associated East/Central/South African (ECSA) virus lineage and dated the origin of the sampled Guangdong outbreak lineage from late April to early May 2025. The interval between the estimated origin of the outbreak lineage and the first reported case was consistent with a period of undetected local transmission and exposed limitations in passive surveillance for early arboviral outbreak detection. Spatiotemporal reconstruction showed two distinct epidemic waves with contrasting transmission dynamics. The Foshan wave involved frequent medium- to long-distance viral movement, while the Jiangmen wave remained relatively localized. Together, these findings reconstruct the early establishment and spatially heterogeneous spread of the largest documented CHIKV epidemic in southern China to date and demonstrate the necessity of expanding active genomic surveillance in areas at the fringe of CHIKV endemic transmission for timely detecting and characterizing emerging epidemics.

papers.title: Hidden overweight and adverse birth outcomes among Asian mothers in the United States, 2016-2023: a population-based repeated cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Background: Standard body mass index (BMI) categories may understate risk in Asian individuals. Lower Asian action points exist, but their relevance to birth outcomes is unclear. Objectives: To estimate the proportion of normal-weight Asian mothers with BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2 and its association with birth outcomes, overall and by Asian subgroup, and to compare Asian and White mothers. Methods: Repeated cross-sectional study of US singleton live births, 2016-2023 (National Vital Statistics System). Outcomes were hypertensive disorders, caesarean delivery, preterm birth, and low birthweight. Modified Poisson regression, adjusted for confounders and Asian subgroup, estimated risk ratios (RRs), standardized risks, and risk differences (RDs). We tested for a change in slope at 23.0 kg/m2, subgroup heterogeneity, and race x BMI interaction. Results: Among 1,758,116 non-Hispanic Asian mothers, 314,510 (17.9%) had BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2, 30.4% of normal-weight mothers. Compared with BMI 18.5-22.9, standardized risk of hypertensive disorders was 4.5% versus 3.2% (RD 1.4 percentage points, 95% CI 1.3, 1.5; RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.40, 1.47), and of caesarean delivery 32.4% versus 28.6% (RR 1.14, 95% CI 1.13, 1.14). Preterm birth risk was 7.2% versus 6.6% (RR 1.08, 95% CI 1.06, 1.10); low birthweight risk was not higher (7.1% versus 7.5%; RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.93, 0.97). The hypertensive-disorder slope showed no evidence of change at 23.0 (ratio of per-unit RRs 0.99, 95% CI 0.98, 1.01); the hypertensive-disorder RR ranged from 1.24 (95% CI 1.18, 1.29) among Asian Indian to 1.70 (95% CI 1.60, 1.81) among Chinese mothers. BMI-outcome associations differed between Asian and White mothers. Conclusions: Nearly one in three normal-weight Asian mothers had BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2, associated with higher risks of hypertensive disorders and caesarean delivery but not low birthweight. The hypertensive-disorder gradient showed no evidence of change at 23.0 kg/m2, and associations varied across Asian subgroups.

papers.title: Time to sustained control of the effective reproduction number as a failure-time estimand: a county-level analysis of the first SARS-CoV-2 wave in the United States.
papers.abstract: Subnational analyses of emerging pathogen transmission typically model the reproduction number (Rt) as a continuous outcome and estimate average associations with its level. Operationally, however, response planning depends on a different quantity: which jurisdictions bring transmission below the epidemic threshold (Rt<1), and how quickly. We formulate time to control as a failure-time estimand and show that doing so exposes a structural feature that linear regression does not accommodate: a jurisdiction cannot enter the risk set until enough cases accumulate to estimate Rt. Cases accumulate faster where transmission is faster, so entry time depends on the outcome process itself and on factors that drive early spread. We account for this outcome-dependent observability using a mixed-effects Cox proportional hazards model with calendar-time left truncation and state-level Gaussian frailties, applied to 2,956 US counties observed between January 22 and July 15, 2020. The primary event was defined as the first three-day sustained reduction of mean Rt below one. Control was rare (171 counties, 5.8%). Each standard-deviation increase in log population density was associated with a lower rate of control (hazard ratio 0.54; 95% confidence interval 0.44 - 0.67) and higher policy stringency with a faster rate (HR 1.50; CI 1.09 - 2.05). Evaluating jurisdictions by their rate of reaching an operational target - rather than by average transmission level - provides a clearer, decision-relevant metric for prospective allocation decisions and public health interventions. Keywords: SARS-CoV-2, COVID-19, reproduction number, survival analysis, Cox model, county-level, United States, policy stringency, population density.

papers.title: Foundation models capture human and environmental context to improve dengue forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate and timely probabilistic dengue forecasts can support public health preparedness, but producing reliable forecasts across locations and time horizons remains challenging. We evaluated five statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and foundation-model approaches for forecasting monthly reported dengue cases across 5,570 Brazilian municipalities at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month horizons, with forecasts backtested from January 2020 to August 2025. The time-series foundation model TimesFM maintained comparatively stable probabilistic forecast performance at longer horizons, while most other models showed declining performance. We then tested whether spatial representations of human and environmental context from a Population Dynamics Foundation Model (PDFM) could improve forecasts through post-hoc residual adjustment. PDFM adjustment improved mean probabilistic forecast performance, measured by the Weighted Interval Score (WIS), in 19 of 20 model-horizon combinations, although the magnitude and frequency of improvements varied across models, horizons and municipalities. The largest improvements were observed for N-BEATS, including a reduction in mean WIS of 1.13 at the six-month horizon (95% CI [0.84, 1.48]; Diebold-Mariano p < 0.0001), with improvements also observed for XGBoost. The proportion of forecasts improved by PDFM generally increased with locally reported dengue case counts, although this relationship varied between models. Covariate selection, spatial fitting and forecast aggregation strategies showed strong model-dependent effects, while monthly model retraining provided no consistent advantage in the settings evaluated. Together, these findings highlight the potential of pretrained representations for dengue forecasting, with benefits dependent on forecasting architecture, horizon and modelling configuration.

papers.title: Quantifying the contribution of policy measures to COVID-19 dynamics across 126 countries
papers.abstract: COVID-19 provides an unprecedented opportunity to evaluate the contribution of public health and social measures (PHSMs) to controlling transmission and inform responses to future emerging respiratory pathogens. We analysed SARS-CoV-2 transmission across 126 countries spanning multiple epidemic waves and diverse policy environments during periods when PHSMs were the primary interventions available to influence the epidemic. By explicitly representing key epidemiological drivers of transmission and measuring reductions in residual transmission scaling after incorporating OxCGRT policy time-series data, we isolated the effect of PHSMs on transmission. PHSMs frequently explained a substantial proportion of the observed variation in transmission intensity, with particularly strong effects seen in many high-income countries. In countries with strong evidence for policy effects, reductions in transmission reached 60-80% or above, although the individual policies responsible for these effects varied considerably. Harmonised analyses considering the effect of community mobility showed comparably strong effects in a similar subset of countries.

papers.title: Estimation of fine-scale spatial heterogeneity in treatment effects in a large cluster-randomized trial
papers.abstract: Treatment effects in randomized trials may vary geographically, and estimating this variation is a broadly generalizable problem for large-scale, cluster-randomized trials. We conducted a secondary analysis of AVENIR, a cluster-randomized, placebo-controlled trial of biannual azithromycin distribution among children aged 1-59 months in Dosso, Niger (2020-2023). We assessed whether the survival benefit of mass azithromycin distribution varied geographically using Poisson models to estimate spatially continuous child mortality and average treatment effects (ATE). Among 1390 villages (276,452 person-years; 3635 deaths), the overall mortality rate was 13.1 and the ATE was -2.6 deaths per 1000 person-years. Mortality was highest in the south, whereas treatment benefit was concentrated in the southeast, following a northwest-southeast gradient. Aggregation of data to 160 primary health catchment areas preserved broad spatial patterns in mortality but attenuated local heterogeneity, suggesting that health catchment monitoring is sufficient for broad mortality surveillance. Examining unit-level, spatially predicted treatment effects as a function of mortality rate demonstrated that underlying mortality captured much, but not all, of the heterogeneity in treatment effects. The analysis demonstrates how to estimate localized treatment effects in large cluster-randomized trials and provides new insights into spatial heterogeneity in mortality and benefits of azithromycin distribution in Niger.

papers.title: Housing Tenure and Mental Health Across Adulthood: Evidence from the 1970 British Birth Cohort
papers.abstract: Background In the UK, declining home ownership and delayed entry into the housing market have reshaped patterns of housing tenure (whether people own or rent their homes) across adulthood. Home ownership may reflect socioeconomic advantage, but may also provide greater housing security, stability and control, with implications for mental health. Using data from the 1970 British Cohort Study (BCS70), this study examines how home ownership trajectories, defined by whether, when and for how long individuals own their homes, are associated with mental health in midlife. Methods We analysed data from 8,016 BCS70 participants with information on housing tenure histories and mental health outcomes at age 51. Housing tenure was measured repeatedly from ages 26 to 46 and used to define prespecified patterns of home ownership across adulthood (referred to as ownership regimes), including sustained ownership and never owning. Mental health outcomes at age 51 were psychological distress and positive mental wellbeing. G-estimation of a structural nested mean model was used to estimate contrasts between these ownership regimes while accounting for time-varying confounding affected by prior exposure. Models were estimated in lavaan; non-response weights and full information maximum likelihood were used to address selective attrition and missing data. Results At age 51, 71% of participants owned their home (23% outright and 48% with a mortgage), while 24% were renting and 5% lived in other arrangements. Sustained home ownership across adulthood was associated with lower psychological distress at age 51 compared with never owning (ATE -0.21, 95% CI -0.47 to -0.03) and higher positive mental wellbeing (ATE 0.56 SD, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.67). In ownership-history regime contrasts, late ownership (first ownership in one's 40s) was associated with lower psychological distress than never owning (ATE -0.15, 95% CI -0.30 to -0.04), while the estimate for early ownership (first ownership in one's 30s) was in the same direction but imprecise (ATE -0.12, 95% CI -0.37 to 0.04). For wellbeing, both late and early ownership were associated with higher scores than never owning (ATE 0.17 SD, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.27 and ATE 0.40 SD, 95% CI 0.24 to 0.51, respectively), with the largest association observed for sustained ownership. Conclusion Home ownership across adulthood (age 26 to 46) was associated with better mental health in midlife (age 51) after accounting for time-varying socio-economic and health-related confounding. Findings suggest that both the timing and persistence of ownership may matter, particularly for positive mental wellbeing, with more sustained exposure to ownership associated with more favourable outcomes.

papers.title: Estimating duration in sex work from cross-sectional studies: a Bayesian global synthesis suggests shorter durations
papers.abstract: Durations selling sex are key determinants of HIV/STI transmission dynamics and service coverage. Such durations are usually estimated from cross-sectional surveys of people actively selling sex. However, cross-sectional surveys are more likely to include individuals selling sex for longer, and survey-reported durations will be right-censored. Prior works have not adequately addressed these two competing biases. In this paper, we derive the mathematical relationship between the distribution of durations reported in cross-sectional surveys and the distribution of true durations in the population overall. These distributions will be identical if true durations are exponentially distributed; otherwise, reported durations will typically underestimate the variance in true durations. We develop a parametric Bayesian model of this relationship, and apply it to re-analyze aggregate data from a global systematic review. Our model-estimated average true durations selling sex are significantly shorter than previously published for all regions - e.g. in Africa: 2.1 (95% CI: 1.8-2.5) versus 5.5 years; in Asia: 1.4 (1.2-1.5) versus 2.8-4.0 years. Shorter average durations then suggest that HIV incidence in sex work could be higher than previously thought, to match the same HIV prevalence data. Our approach can be applied beyond sex work, to characterize duration distributions for any transient risk/disease state.

papers.title: Before AI tells patients what to eat, it needs to know where they live: a cross-sectional ecological study of diabetes and food access in California and Michigan census tracts, with a spotlight on Metro Detroit and Metro Los Angeles
papers.abstract: Background: AI chatbots now give people with diabetes diet advice, but whether those foods can be bought near home is rarely checked. Methods: In a cross-sectional ecological study of 11,974 California and Michigan census tracts, I linked diabetes prevalence (CDC PLACES 2025) with two USDA food-access maps: all SNAP-authorized stores (2025) and large grocery stores only (2019). I identified double-burden tracts (high diabetes and low income/low access) and hidden food deserts (low access to large grocery stores, but not to any SNAP store). In a pilot, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude generated meal plans for the same person across 20 high-diabetes tracts in Metro Los Angeles and Metro Detroit; I scored whether advice was healthy and whether foods were sold at nearby store types. Results: Double-burden tracts were few (71 in California, 19 in Michigan), almost none in the two metros. Food-desert tracts had a 1.5 percentage-point higher diabetes prevalence (95% CI, 1.0-2.0). Counting all SNAP stores hid 567 Californian and 329 Michigan food deserts; in Metro Detroit, all 97 disappeared, including 51 high-diabetes tracts with about 19,500 adults with diabetes. Chatbot advice was healthy, but in hidden tracts 30% of recommended foods were not reliably sold nearby; the chatbots barely adjusted. Of 55 places they named, 13% had errors, and most were over a mile away. Conclusions: The current USDA map obscures food deserts, especially in Detroit, and AI diet advice barely adjusts for them. AI nutrition tools for diabetes should include a place-aware check built on public food-access data.

papers.title: High vaccine coverage and non-pharmaceutical interventions decreased hospitalizations and deaths due to the Omicron variant in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
papers.abstract: The Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador (NL) had high vaccination coverage, and few infections were reported prior to the establishment of the Omicron variant. We investigated whether changes in the timing and rate of booster dose administration could have reduced severe disease outcome and reliance on non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during the Omicron wave in NL. We used a vaccination-stratified epidemiological model calibrated to serology data to investigate the impact of vaccination relative to counterfactual vaccination strategies under actual, strict and no NPI scenarios. Compared with a Canadian vaccination rate scenario, the actual vaccination rollout in NL was estimated to have prevented approximately 519 hospitalizations and 122 deaths from December 15, 2021 to December 15, 2022, corresponding to reductions of 25.9% and 30.9%, respectively. These reductions reflected contributions from NL's higher initial primary series coverage (81.3%), higher final booster dose coverage (57.3%), and the implementation of various NPIs for 89 days after the Omicron BA.1 variant became established. Earlier and faster administration of booster doses reduced the duration of strict NPIs required to achieve hospitalization targets. Our findings show how the timing and rate of vaccination rollout can complement NPIs to reduce severe disease and the duration for which strict NPIs are required.

papers.title: Pandemic-Driven Shifts in RSV Diversity, Evolution, and Global Spread
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic dramatically disrupted the seasonal circulation of RSV, with subsequent heterogeneous global resurgence. We aimed to characterize how pandemic-era disruptions restructured global RSV transmission dynamics, evolutionary patterns, and drivers of reemergence. We show that RSV-A and RSV-B genetic diversity underwent profound pandemic-associated suppression followed by heterogeneous resurgence. The post-pandemic period was characterized by pronounced changes in diversity, with the emergence of novel RSV-A genotypes (A.D.3 and A.D.5.2) and the expansion of the RSV-B, B.D.E.1 genotype. The recovery of RSV-B deviated strongly from neutral expectations and positive selection was detected at 20 sites in the G glycoprotein, F fusion protein, and M2-2 regulatory protein. Phylogeographic reconstruction revealed a sharp decline in international viral spread during the pandemic, followed by increasing persistence. Europe consistently served as the predominant global source, followed by Western Pacific and North America. Air-travel volume was the strongest predictor of dissemination (log coefficient >0.68 for both subtypes). Post-pandemic RSV resurgence represented fundamental epidemiological restructuring shaped by a population bottleneck, positive selection and major impact of air-travel. These findings underscore the need for robust genomic surveillance to track the global circulation of lineages, and to monitor effectiveness of pharmaceutical interventions given the emergence of new genotypes.

papers.title: Biomarkers of ageing and lung function trajectory: a multi-omics study in a UK birth cohort
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accelerated biological ageing and cellular senescence are pathogenically implicated in COPD and may represent therapeutic targets. Adverse early-life lung function trajectories offer opportunities to prevent COPD but their relationship with epigenetic and proteomic ageing biomarkers remains unexplored. We investigated using conventional epidemiological and Mendelian randomisation (MR) methods. METHODS: Outcomes were the two lowest of five FEV1 trajectories (Persistently Low and Below Average) previously identified using latent profile analysis (ages 8-30) in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children. Exposures included nine measures of blood-derived epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and thirteen senescence-associated plasma proteins (ages 7-9). We used logistic regression to estimate odds of lower trajectory membership by exposure and bidirectional one-sample MR to investigate causation. RESULTS: Higher plasma CXCL10 (OR 1.29 per SD; 95% CI 1.03, 1.57), IL6 (OR 1.29; 1.03, 1.57) and IL33 (OR 1.23; 1.04, 1.44) were associated with Persistently Low lung function trajectory, with little evidence for associations between EAA and lower trajectories. MR provided little evidence that genetically predicted plasma proteins influenced risk of lower trajectories, but lower genetically proxied childhood FEV1 predicted higher plasma CXCL10 at ages 9 ({beta} -0.34; -0.65, -0.03) and 24 ({beta} -0.38; -0.67, -0.08). INTERPRETATION: Childhood plasma CXCL10, IL6 and IL33, but not EAA, predict low lung function trajectory into early adulthood. Lower childhood lung function may causally relate to persistently increased plasma CXCL10. Future research should investigate IL33 as a potential therapeutic target in low lung function trajectory and persistent systemic inflammation as a mechanism for associated multimorbidity.

papers.title: Spatial distribution and factors associated with unmet need for family planning among women of reproductive age in Zambia: Evidence from the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey
papers.abstract: Unmet need for family planning contributes to unintended pregnancies, unsafe abortions, and preventable maternal and child deaths, and remains high in sub-Saharan Africa. In Zambia, national estimates may conceal important geographic inequalities. We assessed the spatial distribution of unmet need for family planning among women of reproductive age in Zambia and the factors associated with it. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey (ZDHS), including 12,133 women aged 15-49 years. We used survey-weighted logistic regression, accounting for the stratified two-stage cluster design, to estimate adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Global spatial autocorrelation was assessed with Morans I, local hotspots with the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic, and spatial clusters with a purely spatial Bernoulli scan statistic in SaTScan. The weighted prevalence of unmet need was 27.0% (95% CI: 25.7-28.3%), ranging from 23.8% in Central to 31.6% in North-Western Province. Unmet need was spatially clustered (Morans I = 0.142, p = 0.018), with hotspots mainly in Lusaka, Southern, North-Western, and Northern provinces; SaTScan detected a primary cluster in Lusaka (observed-to-expected ratio 1.42, p < 0.001). Women in union (AOR 2.33, 95% CI: 1.90-2.86) and never-married women (AOR 2.20, 95% CI: 1.69-2.86) had higher odds of unmet need than formerly married women, as did women with five or more children compared with none (AOR 3.05, 95% CI: 2.25-4.13). Lower odds were observed among women aged 35-49 years (AOR 0.65, 95% CI: 0.52-0.83), women in the richest wealth quintile (AOR 0.62, 95% CI: 0.45-0.86), employed women (AOR 0.73, 95% CI: 0.64-0.84) and urban residents (AOR 0.80, 95% CI: 0.68-0.95). Unmet need for family planning in Zambia is high, geographically clustered and socially patterned. Family planning programmes should prioritise hotspot areas, particularly Lusaka, Southern and North-Western provinces, while targeting younger, higher-parity and poorer women.

papers.title: Determinants of Binge Drinking Among Current Alcohol Drinkers: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the 2013 Health and Welfare Survey
papers.abstract: This cross sectional analytical study examined the prevalence and determinants of binge drinking (BD) among current alcohol drinkers (CAD) aged 20 years and older in Thailand (N = 52,847). Data from the Health and Welfare Surveys (HWS) were analyzed using chi square tests and multiple logistic regression. In 2013, nearly 69% of the 5,445 current drinkers reported BD. Multivariable analyses indicated significantly higher odds of BD among men (AOR = 2.25, 95% CI: 1.90-2.66; p < 0.001), younger adults (AOR range: 1.50-1.90; p < 0.001), individuals with household housing expenses (AOR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.01-1.39; p < 0.05), and those with secondary/vocational or tertiary education (AOR range: 1.35-1.36; p < 0.05). Smoking was also associated with elevated odds of BD (AOR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.23-1.62; p < 0.001). In contrast, respondents in high income groups had lower odds (AOR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.54-0.87; p < 0.01), as did residents of non metropolitan areas compared with Bangkok (AOR range: 0.44-0.59; p < 0.01). In conclusion, binge drinking affected over half of Thai drinkers and was strongly linked to demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and behavioral factors. The frequent co-occurrence of alcohol use and smoking underscores the clustering of non-communicable disease risks, highlighting the need for integrated dual-cessation programs. While cross-sectional design and 2013 data limitations apply, these findings provide actionable evidence for public health agencies to implement targeted screening and intervention strategies for high-risk populations.

papers.title: The origin of the MV Hondius Andes outbreak
papers.abstract: In April-July 2026, Andes virus (ANDV) caused an outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulting in 12 confirmed cases and three deaths. Before symptom onset, the index case had travelled through hantavirus-endemic regions of Chile and Argentina, leaving the geographic origin of infection unresolved. We conducted phylogenetic and phylogeographic analyses using newly generated ANDV genomes from human cases and rodent reservoirs to investigate the likely origin of the outbreak. Through phylogenetic analyses, we show that the outbreak genome falls within a geographically structured lineage spanning southern Chile and Argentine Andean Patagonia. Using phylogeographic reconstructions across all three segments, integrated with the index cases travel itinerary, we identified the Tolten-Lanco area of southern Chile as the most likely geographic origin of the outbreak genome, with two candidate locations accounting for >98% of the posterior support. However, the index case visited this area 62-66 days before symptom onset, exceeding the conventionally reported ANDV incubation period of 7-42 days. Thus, while genomic evidence supports a southern Chilean origin of the outbreak genome, the timing and circumstances of transmission to the index case remain unresolved.

papers.title: Defining ocular Chlamydia trachomatis infection prevalence thresholds for the trachoma elimination endgame
papers.abstract: Trachoma is the leading infectious cause of blindness worldwide and is targeted for global elimination as a public health problem by 2030. As we approach this target, defining when population-level trachoma control interventions can be stopped, and determining how post-intervention surveillance should be performed, are becoming increasingly important. Molecular diagnosis of ocular Chlamydia trachomatis (Ct) using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) provides a highly sensitive and specific indicator of infection, yet there are currently no programmatic guidelines based on Ct infection. We assembled 86 cross-sectional surveys of ocular Ct infection from 13 countries, representing data from 46,914 children aged 1-5 years. Our analyses suggest that infection prevalence of 0.81% in this age group corresponds to a threshold below which population-level interventions can be stopped with at least 90% confidence. Correspondingly, with confidence exceeding 90%, we propose that interventions should continue when infection prevalence is greater than 1.99%. Interpretation of infection surveillance data is a generalisable challenge in low-prevalence settings for many infectious diseases. This study proposes a robust framework for how Ct infection surveillance could support accurate population-level assessments of trachoma endemicity and could allow a step-change in decision-making precision for programmes as we approach the endgame for trachoma elimination.

papers.title: Evaluating methods to quantify the effect of deprescribing a medication on patient clinical outcomes using a simulation study
papers.abstract: Observational studies using electronic health records are being increasingly used to answer research questions of interest in deprescribing, where a medication is intentionally discontinued or the dose reduced. Target trial emulation (TTE) is particularly attractive as it is guided by sound theoretical principles based on causal inference. In the field of deprescribing, the evaluation of TTE within a simulation setting can provide evidence on optimal approaches for implementation and compare different estimation approaches which theory cannot easily inform. Deprescribing studies are susceptible to time-dependent confounding, competing risks due to early adverse events, time-dependent effects and other data complexities which may render estimates biased if such aspects are not properly addressed. In this work, a Monte-Carlo simulation study was conducted to estimate the performance (bias and coverage) of seven methods within several synthetic data generating mechanisms involving the above characteristics. The methods implemented were Cox regression, inverse probability of treatment weighted (IPTW) Cox regression, naive sequential Cox regression, IPTW weighted sequential Cox regression, extended Cox regression and the parametric g-formula. The IPTW Cox regression and IPTW sequential Cox regression were the only methods achieving nominal coverage and unbiasedness under the scenarios evaluated.

papers.title: Socio-economic inequalities and cancer mortality among adolescents and young adults between 2000 and 2023
papers.abstract: Cancer among adolescents and young adults (AYAs) has been a growing public health concern in France since 2009, a priority reaffirmed in the new 2026-2030 roadmap of the Ten-Year Cancer Control Strategy. This issue is also generating increasing interest internationally, as evidenced by the emergence of scientific conferences dedicated to this population. However, the socioeconomic inequalities associated with cancer mortality among AYAs remain insufficiently documented internationally. The objective of this study is to analyze the socioeconomic determinants associated with cancer mortality among AYAs. Epidemiological data on cancer patients aged 15 to 39 are available for 37 countries for 2000 to 2023, these data being drawn from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD 2023) databases. For this study, they were supplemented by socioeconomic indicators from the United Nations Development Program and the World Bank. Descriptive analyses, correlations, principal component analysis, classification methods, time-series trend analyses (EAPC and Joinpoint), and panel data models have been performed. Results highlight a strong socioeconomic gradient in mortality. High-income countries have an average standardized mortality rate of 1.5 per 100,000 inhabitants, compared to 3.7 per 100,000 inhabitants in lower-middle-income countries. The mortality-to-incidence ratio decreases from 0.45 to 0.15 with increasing income level. Multivariate analyses confirm a significant association between the Human Development Index and cancer mortality among adolescents and young adults (AYAs), after adjusting for other model variables. Joinpoint analyses also reveal heterogeneous temporal trends according to sex and cancer type. This study highlights importance of socio-economic determinants in international inequalities in cancer mortality among AYAs.

papers.title: Maternal ADHD and exclusive breastfeeding: A prospective community-based cohort study
papers.abstract: ImportanceMaternal attention-deficit disorder with or without hyperactivity (ADHD) is an established risk factor for adverse perinatal outcomes that remains understudied to breastfeeding. ObjectiveTo estimate the effect of maternal ADHD on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding. DesignA prospective longitudinal community-based cohort study. SettingCanada, 2014-2020. ParticipantsWe included 3217 English-literate mother-father dyads with internet or telephone access, comprising women with singleton birth within 3 weeks postpartum (study baseline) and were cohabiting with the biological father. Women with major psychiatric conditions or suicidality were excluded. All participants provided informed consent at recruitment. Data were collected online through self-report questionnaires. ExposureMaternal ADHD was measured at baseline using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (sum of scores [≥]14). Main Outcomes and MeasuresWe defined 6-month exclusive breastfeeding based on maternal reported infant feeding, assessed at 3 and 6 months. Maternal childhood adversity (Adverse Childhood Experiences International Questionnaire, ACE-IQ; sum score) was included as a confounder. The average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) was estimated using linear probability models. We calculated 95% percentile bootstrap CI. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation by chained equations with 10 iterations. ResultsComplete-case analyses included 2071/3217 mother-father dyads, most of which were Canadian-born (79%). Childhood adversity, mental health conditions, and substance use were higher among mothers who screened positive for ADHD (4%) than among those who did not: the median number of ACE was 5 IQR 4-6; 38% self-reported prenatal depression, 13% smoked cigarettes and 19% drank alcohol during pregnancy; 11% of infants used the neonatal intensive care unit. Notably, though 90% of mothers with ADHD intended to breastfeed exclusively only 28% breastfed exclusively for 6 months. Among families with maternal ADHD, the effect of maternal ADHD on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding was ATT -0.105, 95% CI -0.209 to -0.003 in the model adjusted for maternal ACE and paternal ADHD. With multiple imputation: ATT -0.109, 95% CI -0.213 to -0.004. Conclusions and RelevanceMothers with ADHD intend to breastfeed their infants exclusively, but additional challenges shorten the duration of exclusive breastfeeding, indicating a need for interventions tailored to neurodevelopmental differences. KEY POINTSO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSDoes maternal ADHD influence exclusive breastfeeding duration? FindingsIn this community-based cohort study of 3217 mother-father dyads in Canada, most mothers with ADHD intended to breastfeed exclusively, but few actually maintained it for 6 months. Maternal ADHD predicted lower probability of exclusive breastfeeding until 6 months among families with maternal ADHD. MeaningTo equitably promote maternal and infant well-being, early detection and support for breastfeeding challenges are needed for mothers with ADHD.

papers.title: Association between trajectories of breastfeeding duration and infant health: Prospective cohort study
papers.abstract: BackgroundBreastfeeding is a modifiable pathway contributing to infant health. ObjectivesTo estimate trajectories of breastfeeding and the association between trajectories of breastfeeding and infant health. MethodsWe conducted a prospective longitudinal cohort study (2014-2020, Canada) with 3217 cohabitating English-literate mother-father-infant triads with internet or telephone access. Women with major psychiatric conditions or suicidality were excluded. Data were collected online at baseline ( 90th percentile). We estimated trajectories of breastfeeding using latent class growth analysis. Associations were estimated using adjusted linear mixed models. ResultsMost included mothers (n=2548) were of Canadian birth (2078/2548, 82%) and graduated from university (1920/2548, 75%); few reported unemployment (222/2548, 9%) or prenatal depression (240/2548, 9%). We identified two trajectories of breastfeeding: Constant Breastfeeding (1522/2548, 60%) and Decreasing Breastfeeding (1026/2548, 40%). No statistically significant differences were observed between classes for either the risk of challenging behaviors (RR -0.006 95% CI -0.028 to 0.016) or the risk of emergent visits (RR -0.015 95% CI -0.053 to 0.023). ConclusionsIn this study, discontinued breastfeeding was not associated with infant health. Future studies should focus on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding, a modifiable therapeutic infant feeding target. Article SummaryIn this prospective community-based cohort of 2548 Canadian mother-father-infant triads, we observed that maternal lifetime risk factors of depression - ADHD and childhood adversity - were associated with increased risk of infant morbidity from 12-24 months, but not decreasing vs. constant breastfeeding from 0-12 months. Breastfeeding duration was not significantly associated with infant morbidity.

papers.title: Target Trial Emulation of Metformin for Dementia Prevention in All of Us: Robustness to Cohort and Confounder Definitions
papers.abstract: Metformin use has been associated with a lower risk of incident dementia than other antidiabetics. We perform target trial emulation and causal competing risk analysis in the NIH All of Us (AoU) Research Program database, contrasting the effects of metformin and sulfonylurea initiation on dementia onset and death without dementia. AoU's social and behavioral health data allowed us to test robustness to excluding such confounders, and we further adjusted for calendar year effects and prior antidiabetic exposure, using both semiparametric Cox proportional hazards (PH) models and nonparametric models. Under stabilized inverse propensity score of treatment weighting, metformin was associated with a substantially lower risk of death (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.61, 95% CI: [0.49, 0.75]) and a lower incidence of dementia (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: [0.82, 1.02]). Estimated HRs were closely aligned with estimates obtained in the UK primary care and US Mass General Brigham health systems. This finding was robust to the inclusion of participants without a type 2 diabetes diagnosis at baseline and to the consideration of different covariate sets in the propensity score model, supporting metformin as a promising candidate for dementia prevention and motivating prospective validation.

papers.title: Suicide in young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) in England 2011 to 2022: A retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: BackgroundPopulation-level evidence on suicide mortality among children and young people (CYP) with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) is limited. SEND captures a broad and heterogeneous population, including children whose needs are recognised in educational settings regardless of recorded clinical diagnosis. MethodsWe analysed 3,959,390 CYP aged 10-18 years in England using GUiE data linked to death registrations. SEND provision was classified as "no support", "support" or "statement", using records from academic years 2001/02 to 2010/11. CYP were followed until age 25, death or 31 December 2022. Sex-stratified, age-adjusted Cox models estimated suicide by SEND provision. ResultsIn the cohort, 1,383,300 CYP (35%) had provision of support and 148,200 (4%) had a statement. During follow-up, 2,620 suicides occurred among 10- to 24-year-olds; 1,190 (45.4%) were among CYP with support and 130 (5%) among those with statements. Compared with males with no support, suicide was higher among males with provision of support (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.33-1.61) and statements (HR: 1.32; 95% CI: 1.09-1.61). Among females, support provision was associated with higher risk of suicide (HR: 1.23; 95% CI: 1.05-1.44), while no significant difference was observed for those with statements (HR: 1.15; 95% CI: 0.69-1.92). Suicide rates were highest among CYP with social, emotional and mental health needs. ConclusionsCYP with SEND had elevated risk of suicide, particularly those receiving support without a statutory plan and those with social, emotional and mental health needs, highlighting the need for targeted prevention.

papers.title: Canada's loss of measles elimination after 27 years: a mathematical modelling analysis of the five major provincial outbreak waves in 2025-2026
papers.abstract: BackgroundCanadas loss of measles elimination status in 2025 highlighted the vulnerability of populations with concentrated immunity gaps. Provincial incidence alone cannot readily distinguish relatively intense transmission within a small susceptible population from transmission involving a larger population. We quantified these differences across five provincial measles waves in 2025-2026. MethodsWe fitted a common susceptible-exposed-infectious-recovered (SEIR) model to weekly reported measles incidence for Ontario in 2025 and Alberta and Manitoba in 2025 and 2026. Mean latent and infectious periods were fixed at 10 and 8 days. We estimated the effective reproduction number (Reff,0), effective susceptible population (Seff,0), and profiled the initial infected number to evaluate province and wave-specific primary case model estimates. We calculate the initial exponential growth rate, doubling time, and peak full width at half maximum (FWHM) to characterize early epidemic growth and the duration of elevated incidence around each waves peak. FindingsIn 2025, Ontarios effective reproduction number, Reff,0, was 1.9, with a model-estimated effective susceptible population, Seff,0, of 3,101 individuals, an initial doubling time of 2.4 weeks, and a peak FWHM of 12.3 weeks. Alberta had a similar Reff,0 of 1.9, with Seff,0 of 2,601 individuals, a doubling time of 2.4 weeks, and FWHM of 12.1 weeks. Manitoba had a lower Reff,0 of 1.5 and Seff,0 of 490 individuals, with a longer doubling time of 4.0 weeks and FWHM of 20.5 weeks. In 2026, Albertas Reff,0 increased to 2.1 while Seff,0 decreased to 383 individuals; doubling time shortened to 2.1 weeks and FWHM to 9.7 weeks. Manitobas Reff,0 increased to 1.8 and Seff,0 to 1,038 individuals, while doubling time shortened to 2.6 weeks and FWHM to 13.0 weeks. InterpretationAlbertas smaller second wave combined the highest effective reproduction number with the shortest doubling time and peak duration, demonstrating that limited outbreak size can coexist with rapid transmission. Joint estimates of transmission intensity, epidemic pace, peak duration, and effective susceptible population provide complementary measures for comparing outbreaks and informing public-health planning. Together, these estimates provide a quantitative basis for distinguishing transmission intensity from the scale of susceptible involvement, supporting comparisons across outbreaks and informing the timing and scale of public-health responses for future outbreaks.

papers.title: Allostatic load as a potential pathway linking exposomic risk to early-onset cancer: a matched case-control study in the All of Us Research Program
papers.abstract: BackgroundEarly-onset cancer (EoC) incidence is rising worldwide, yet risk models built on isolated exposures or rare pathogenic variants capture little of the cumulative environmental burden experienced by younger adults. Allostatic load (AL), the cumulative physiological burden of chronic stress, can be measured from routine laboratory values and vital signs and is a candidate biological pathway linking environmental exposures to carcinogenesis. MethodsWe conducted a 1:4 matched case-control study nested within the NIH All of Us Research Program, including 7,550 participants and 1,510 cancers diagnosed before age 50, of which 298 were exposome-related (the primary outcome). We derived an exposomic risk score (ERS) from 12 survey-based measures and an eight-component AL score from electronic health record data, and used mediation analysis to estimate the proportion of the ERS-EoC association operating through AL. ResultsA higher ERS was associated with higher AL ({beta}=0.18 standard deviations [SD] per SD; 95% CI 0.16-0.20), and each SD increase in AL was associated with 21% higher odds of EoC (odds ratio 1.21; 95% CI 1.15-1.28). For exposome-related EoC, AL mediated 17.4% (95% CI 8.2-44.7%) of the association between the ERS and EoC, with significant total, direct, and indirect effects that were robust to sensitivity analyses of diagnosis timing, AL scoring, and age adjustment. Across all EoC, the proportion mediated was 48.8% (95% CI 21.2-186.5%). ConclusionsAL is a candidate biomarker and potential pathway through which cumulative environmental burden relates to EoC, warranting prospective validation in independent cohorts.

papers.title: The role of climate and immunity in Brazil unprecedented outbreak of dengue in 2024
papers.abstract: Brazil experienced a large dengue epidemic during the 2024 season, with almost 5.7 million total cases (compared to under 1.3 million in 2023), raising questions about underlying drivers, including rising temperatures, expansion into susceptible populations, changes in reporting, and novel strains. We compared state-level 2024 incidence with 2000-2023 data to quantify anomalies. Nine of 27 states, primarily in the Southeast, recorded their highest incidence in 25 years, accounting for 97% of cases while comprising only 67% of the population. In contrast, nine states (mostly in the North and Northeast) reported below-average incidence. Counterintuitively, the correlation between state-level temperature and incidence declined significantly over the study period, turning negative by 2024 (r = -0.72), a reversal from the positive correlations observed at the start. To determine whether this pattern was driven by northern temperatures being too high for transmission, or by spatial variation in immunity, we fit generalized additive models to effective reproductive numbers. Transmission remained substantial at the highest temperatures, while reproductive numbers declined with lagged cumulative incidences, indicating susceptibility depletion was important. We then estimated state-level susceptibility using a mechanistic SEIR-SEI model, describing a trade-off: high temperatures supported high transmission rates, but were associated with reduced susceptibility. Linear regression models confirmed both temperature and susceptibility were necessary to predict the 2024 outbreaks, suggesting that immunity plays an important role in modulating temperatures effect on incidence. Future surveillance integrating measures of immunity could enhance forecasts and early-warning systems, particularly as climate change expands dengue into immunologically naive populations. Significance StatementBrazil experienced an unprecedented dengue epidemic in 2024, with nearly 5.7 million reported cases. The relative role of high temperature and population immunity in driving this large outbreak remains poorly understood. High temperatures are known to support increased transmission but surprisingly, the relationship between incidence and temperature had turned negative by this outbreak. Our results show that transmission remained viable at the highest temperatures, but outbreaks were constrained by immunity acquired through prior infection. Large epidemics occurred only where favorable temperatures coincided with high remaining susceptibility, itself largely a legacy of past, temperature-driven transmission. These results demonstrate that immunity modulates climate-driven dengue risk, highlighting the value of estimating population immunity alongside climate.

papers.title: Brownfield land and emergency hospital admissions in England: a small-area ecological study using contamination hazard score as an exposure proxy
papers.abstract: BackgroundEmpirical evidence on the health impacts of brownfield land - previously developed land that may be contaminated - remains limited, mainly due to poorly defined exposures and pathways. Here we assessed associations between an area-level contamination hazard score and emergency hospital admissions across England, using the score as a proxy for the potential contamination associated with brownfield land. MethodsWe used Lower-layer Super Output Area (LSOA)-level population-weighted contamination hazard scores in Bayesian hierarchical models to examine the risk of emergency hospital admission (age- and sex-standardised, 2010-2019) with a primary diagnosis of i) all causes (excluding external causes), ii) respiratory diseases, and iii) cardiovascular diseases (CVD). Models were adjusted for deprivation, population density, tobacco expenditure, green space, urbanicity, and ethnicity, and included spatially structured and unstructured random effects to account for residual spatial autocorrelation between neighbouring areas. Stratified analyses assessed potential effect modification by deprivation, urban/rural classification, and region. ResultsWe included 42,875,231 admissions for all natural causes, 6,657,050 for respiratory diseases, and 4,393,461 for CVD across 32,844 LSOAs in England. LSOAs with higher contamination hazard scores showed a non-linear decreasing trend in relative risk (RR) for all health outcomes. Spatial variation was evident, with stronger negative associations in urban and the least deprived LSOAs, while rural and more deprived LSOAs showed weaker associations or greater uncertainty. Region-specific analyses demonstrated inverse associations for all outcomes in London and for all natural causes and respiratory admissions in the North West and East of England. Other regions showed no consistent pattern across outcomes. ConclusionHigher contamination hazard scores were associated with lower emergency hospital admission risks. This suggests that areas with a greater legacy of potentially contaminating land uses do not necessarily experience poorer contemporary population health. The inverse associations may partly reflect subsequent remediation and urban regeneration, although the underlying mechanisms require further investigation. HighlightsO_LIA national brownfield study used contamination hazard scores as an exposure proxy. C_LIO_LIHigher contamination hazard scores were linked to lower emergency admission risks. C_LIO_LIInverse associations were strongest in urban areas, least deprived areas and London. C_LIO_LILower risks may reflect redevelopment, not a protective effect of brownfield land. C_LI

papers.title: Spatially varying effect estimates of mediation in the presence of spatial auto-correlation
papers.abstract: The use of mediation analysis is common in epidemiology to decompose an exposure-outcome total effect into direct and indirect effects via a given set of mediators. The counterfactual framework in causal inference allowed for great improvements in mediation analysis to define identification assumptions and clarify sources of bias in different settings. Multiple mediation methods have been proposed to consider confounders of various types and for different settings such as longitudinal designs. However, in some settings we may reasonably expect spatially heterogeneous estimates of both natural direct and indirect effects. In various research areas, especially environmental and social epidemiology, we would expect there to be spatial dependence that could be leveraged. In this paper, we describe and compare a set of approaches to perform spatial mediation analyses and conduct an extensive set of simulations to quantify their performance. We also present a case study assessing the spatially heterogeneous mediating role of PM2.5 in the association between income and cardiovascular diseases. We provide all code via GitHub for replication and reproducibility purposes. We find that using a framework combining geographically weighted regression (GWR) and other spatially varying coefficient (SVC) models and the product method of mediation analysis is accurate and precise at estimating spatially heterogeneous effect estimates and handling spatial confounding in a grid setting. Such spatial approaches can be extended to any mediation approach and various confounding structures.

papers.title: Concordance with the MIND diet is associated with lower subsequent epigenetic aging
papers.abstract: Abstract/SummaryHealthy dietary patterns may influence biological aging, but prospective evidence for the Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet is limited. We linked 2013 dietary data to 2016 DNA methylation measures in 1,740 Health and Retirement Study participants. Per 1-s.d. higher MIND score, adjusted differences were -0.4 years for PhenoAge acceleration (95% CI -0.8 to -0.1), -0.3 years for GrimAge acceleration (-0.5 to -0.1) and -0.0054 for methylation Pace of Aging (-0.0098 to -0.0010); all false-discovery-rate q[≤]0.026. Associations persisted after body-mass-index adjustment and selection weighting. Targeted maximum likelihood estimates were concordant with the conventional models, whereas causal forests evaluated in held-out and repeated-split samples found no reproducible evidence that specific subgroups of participants benefited more than others. Greater MIND concordance was associated with lower subsequent epigenetic aging across complementary measures, supporting molecular aging as an intermediate phenotype for diet-aging research.

papers.title: 24-hour time-use behaviors and maternal depressive symptoms during early pregnancy: Compositional data analysis
papers.abstract: BackgroundPrevious research suggested that modifiable health factors such as physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep (i.e., 24-hour time-use behaviors) were potential intervention targets to improve antenatal depressive symptoms. However, most previous studies examine one behavior at a time, ignoring their co-dependence. The aim of this study was to examine the association between 24-hour time-use behaviors and depressive symptoms during early pregnancy. MethodsWe conducted a secondary analysis using baseline data from the Health and Behaviors in Transition (HABIT) trial. Pregnant participants with pre-pregnancy body mass index [≥]25 kg/m2 wore a wrist-worn ActiGraph for seven consecutive days to estimate moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), light physical activity (LPA), inactivity (IA), and sleep. We used compositional data analysis with an isometric log-ratio transformation to examine associations with depressive symptoms, quantified by the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), adjusting for maternal age, socioeconomic status, and cohabitation status. G-computation was applied to estimate the marginal mean of depressive symptoms at specified durations of each behavior, with the remaining time reallocated proportionally among the other behaviors. ResultsA total of 255 participants with median EPDS score of 5.0 (IQR, 2.0-8.0) had geometric mean 24-hour behaviors of MVPA = 75.5 min/day (5.2%), LPA = 311.2 min/day (21.6%), IA = 593.9 min/day (41.2%), and sleep = 459.4 min/day (31.9%). 24-hour time-use behaviors were not significantly associated with EPDS scores, and marginal mean EPDS scores showed minimal changes (MVPA 10 min: 6.51 (95% CI 4.22, 9.64) vs 40 min: 5.97 (95% CI 5.03, 6.97); sleep 300 min: 5.41 (95% CI 4.56, 6.22) vs 480 min: 5.81 (95% CI 5.23, 6.39)). ConclusionsIn this relatively active pregnant population, 24-hour time-use behaviors were not associated with depressive symptoms. Future research can examine later trimesters or other populations that are more sedentary or more depressed.
